A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey with the same central taxonomy and case studies. All nine pages of v1 and fourteen pages of v2 are readable, including figures, tables, references, and v2's Appendices A–D. Relocated material can be matched reliably; v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reviews published systems and describes Llama-3 and INTELLECT-1 using attributed training information. It reports no original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. Its new system-comparison table and explanatory appendices compile characteristics of cited work rather than report original empirical results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an executable training method or model. v2 expands and revises descriptions of existing systems, but these are changes to the survey's documentation, not to an algorithm developed by this work.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts dataset-based training or evaluation. The model names newly catalogued in v2 Table 2 describe cited studies, not added experimental coverage. The Llama-3 and INTELLECT-1 case studies are retained.

E2.justification: No methods are experimentally evaluated against a proposed method in either version. Table 1 retains the same three related surveys, while v2's new Table 2 is a literature comparison rather than a baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol is introduced or substantively revised. v2 Table 2 newly documents settings from cited studies. The retained case-study table changes token labels from T to TB, but Section 6 still states 15 T tokens; this is inconsistent documentation rather than an explained training-budget revision.

E4.justification: The same two case studies remain, without new investigative questions or experimental analyses. Appendix C reorganizes the earlier discussion of DHT-based fault tolerance, and Appendix A explains parallelism; neither introduces robustness tests, ablations, or sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures. The additional literature tables do not introduce statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Some secondary reported findings change: v2 Section 4.4 adds that Varuna's approximately fivefold cost advantage preserves throughput, while removing v1's 20% all-optical-network energy-saving statement and Holmes near-homogeneous-performance assertion. Retained figures include StellaTrain's 64.5% cloud-cost reduction and Llama-3's 38–43% MFU. These are edits to surveyed findings, not original experimental gains.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations. v2's added parallelism and DHT explanations are descriptive background. Decentralized scaling laws remain a proposed research direction rather than a derived theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding summary retain the resource-driven framing, community-driven versus organizational taxonomy, optimization-objective classification, two case studies, and future directions. The first-survey novelty claim is also retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds a specific critique of methods overlooking layer sensitivity and gradient rank, and Section 8 identifies missing reasoning-model and vision-language-model-specific treatment. The privacy exclusion already existed. v2 also removes the prediction of a widening centralized/decentralized performance gap and redirects governance discussion from blockchain/game theory toward multi-tenant pricing and scheduling.

D1.justification: New Table 2 substantially expands technical documentation by listing parallel strategies, model sizes, and hardware resources for seventeen cited systems. Sections 4.1–4.3 also expand or revise operational descriptions, without establishing new implementations. Direct Hivemind and Llama-3 model-access links disappear. The relocated case-study table introduces inconsistent TB labels for token counts.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Nebula-I, CloudSimPer, AdaRankGrad, and foundational parallelism work, and refines placement of existing systems within Figures 2–3. Table 1 explicitly describes overlapping paradigms. The main literature framework and novelty positioning remain stable; author, year, and venue updates for matching works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The introduction and resource discussion are extensively rewritten, and communication, heterogeneity, fault-tolerance, and economics passages are reorganized around mechanisms. Sections 2 and 7 are renamed, a limitations section is added, and background plus previously embedded material is organized into Appendices A–D.

P2.justification: v2 adds the system-comparison Table 2 and parallelism Table 3, expands Table 1 with a paradigms column, and lengthens Figure 1's caption. Figures 2–3 are revised and moved into Appendix B; v1 Table 2 becomes Appendix D Table 4. Typography, spacing, and discussion-box presentation also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the survey easier to assess through Table 2's explicit comparison of strategies, model scales, and resources, clearer mechanism explanations, and more specific scope limitations. These improve an otherwise retained taxonomy and set of case studies. The gains are partly offset by the new TB/token inconsistency in Table 4 and remaining unclear prose, supporting a limited overall improvement.
